rules.rule: For safety, `Condvar::init` may only be called once per instance of `Condvar`.

rules.name: unsafe fn init (self : Pin < & mut Self >)
rules.rule: For safety, `Mutex::init` may only be called once per instance of `Mutex`.

rules.name: unsafe fn lock (self : Pin < & Self >)
rules.rule: If `init` was not called on this mutex instance, locking it reentrantly causes undefined behaviour.

rules.name: unsafe fn lock (self : Pin < & Self >)
rules.rule: This mutex must not be destroyed while locked.

rules.name: unsafe fn try_lock (self : Pin < & Self >) -> bool
rules.rule: If `init` was not called on this mutex instance, `try_lock` must not lock it reentrantly; doing so causes undefined behaviour.

rules.name: unsafe fn try_lock (self : Pin < & Self >) -> bool
rules.rule: This mutex must not be destroyed while locked; doing so causes undefined behaviour.

rules.name: unsafe fn unlock (self : Pin < & Self >)
rules.rule: The mutex must be locked by the current thread when `Mutex::unlock` is called.

rules.name: trait SetFileInformation
rules.rule: For an implementation of `SetFileInformation` to be safe, `as_ptr` must return a pointer to memory readable for `size` bytes.

rules.name: trait SetFileInformation
rules.rule: For an implementation of `SetFileInformation` to be safe, `CLASS` must accurately identify the type pointed to by `as_ptr`; for example, `FILE_BASIC_INFO` must use the class `FileBasicInfo`.

rules.name: unsafe fn new (name : & CStr) -> Option < Self >
rules.rule: For safety, `Module::new(name)` must only be used for modules that exist for the lifetime of std.

rules.name: unsafe fn alertable_io_internal (& self , io : impl FnOnce (& mut c :: OVERLAPPED , c :: LPOVERLAPPED_COMPLETION_ROUTINE) -> c :: BOOL ,) -> io :: Result < usize >
rules.rule: `self` must refer to a pipe handle created by this implementation; this API must not be used with handles it did not create.

rules.name: unsafe fn alertable_io_internal (& self , io : impl FnOnce (& mut c :: OVERLAPPED , c :: LPOVERLAPPED_COMPLETION_ROUTINE) -> c :: BOOL ,) -> io :: Result < usize >
rules.rule: The `buf` pointer used by the I/O operation supplied through `io` must point to a buffer valid for reads or writes up to `len` bytes.

rules.name: unsafe fn alertable_io_internal (& self , io : impl FnOnce (& mut c :: OVERLAPPED , c :: LPOVERLAPPED_COMPLETION_ROUTINE) -> c :: BOOL ,) -> io :: Result < usize >
rules.rule: The I/O function used by `io` must be either `ReadFileEx` or `WriteFileEx`.

rules.name: unsafe fn set_name_wide (name : & [u16])
rules.rule: For safety, `name` must end with a zero value.

rules.name: unsafe fn read_encoded_offset (reader : & mut DwarfReader , encoding : u8) -> Result < usize , () >
rules.rule: `encoding` must be a valid DWARF Exception Header Encoding as described by the LSB specification.

rules.name: unsafe fn read_encoded_offset (reader : & mut DwarfReader , encoding : u8) -> Result < usize , () >
rules.rule: The upper ("application") part of `encoding` must be zero.

rules.name: unsafe fn read_encoded_pointer (reader : & mut DwarfReader , context : & EHContext < '_ > , encoding : u8 ,) -> Result < * const u8 , () >
rules.rule: For safety, `encoding` must be a DWARF Exception Header Encoding as described by the LSB specification.

rules.name: unsafe fn read < T : Copy > (& mut self) -> T
rules.rule: Reads of T from the DWARF stream must be performed with alignment 1.

rules.name: unsafe fn new (pid : pid_t , pidfd : pid_t) -> Self
rules.rule: For safety, `pidfd` must be either -1 (representing no file descriptor) or a valid, exclusively owned file descriptor.

rules.name: unsafe fn lock_contested (& self , mut state : u32 , thread_self : zx_handle_t)
rules.rule: For `Mutex::lock_contested` to be safe, `thread_self` must be the handle for the current thread.

rules.name: unsafe fn get_unchecked (& self) -> Pin < & T >
rules.rule: Before calling `OnceBox<T>::get_unchecked`, the value must already be initialized.

rules.name: unsafe fn get_unchecked (& self) -> Pin < & T >
rules.rule: Before calling `OnceBox<T>::get_unchecked`, the current thread must have observed the value's initialization.

rules.name: unsafe fn read_unlock (& self)
rules.rule: To call `RwLock::read_unlock` safely, the `RwLock` must be read-locked (N readers).

rules.name: unsafe fn write_unlock (& self)
rules.rule: To call `RwLock::write_unlock` safely, the `RwLock` must be write-locked with a single writer.

rules.name: unsafe fn downgrade (& self)
rules.rule: To call `RwLock::downgrade` safely, the `RwLock` must be write-locked with a single writer.

rules.name: unsafe fn to_node (state : State) -> NonNull < Node >
rules.rule: The `state` argument must contain a valid pointer to a queue node.

rules.name: unsafe fn wait (& self)
rules.rule: Node::wait may only be called from the thread that created the node.

rules.name: unsafe fn complete (node : NonNull < Node >)
rules.rule: `node` must point to a valid `Node`.

rules.name: unsafe fn complete (node : NonNull < Node >)
rules.rule: The `Node` pointed to by `node` must not outlive this call to `Node::complete`.

rules.name: unsafe fn find_tail_and_add_backlinks (head : NonNull < Node >) -> NonNull < Node >
rules.rule: `head` must point to a node in a valid queue.

rules.name: unsafe fn find_tail_and_add_backlinks (head : NonNull < Node >) -> NonNull < Node >
rules.rule: `head` must be in front of the previous head node that was used to perform the last removal.

rules.name: unsafe fn find_tail_and_add_backlinks (head : NonNull < Node >) -> NonNull < Node >
rules.rule: The part of the queue starting with `head` must not be modified during this call.

rules.name: unsafe fn find_tail_and_add_backlinks (head : NonNull < Node >) -> NonNull < Node >
rules.rule: This function may be called concurrently from multiple threads as long as the queue is not being modified.

rules.name: unsafe fn complete_all (tail : NonNull < Node >)
rules.rule: `tail` must be a valid tail of a fully linked queue.

rules.name: unsafe fn complete_all (tail : NonNull < Node >)
rules.rule: The current thread must have exclusive access to the queue ending with `tail`.

rules.name: unsafe fn read_unlock_contended (& self , state : State)
rules.rule: When calling `RwLock::read_unlock_contended`, there must be threads queued on the lock.

rules.name: unsafe fn read_unlock_contended (& self , state : State)
rules.rule: When calling `RwLock::read_unlock_contended`, `state` must be a pointer to a node in a valid queue.

rules.name: unsafe fn read_unlock_contended (& self , state : State)
rules.rule: When calling `RwLock::read_unlock_contended`, there must not be a `downgrade` in progress.

rules.name: unsafe fn unlock_contended (& self , state : State)
rules.rule: The lock must be exclusively owned by the calling thread when calling `RwLock::unlock_contended`.

rules.name: unsafe fn unlock_contended (& self , state : State)
rules.rule: There must be threads queued on the lock when calling `RwLock::unlock_contended`.

rules.name: unsafe fn unlock_contended (& self , state : State)
rules.rule: The `state` argument to `RwLock::unlock_contended` must be a pointer to a node in a valid queue.

rules.name: unsafe fn unlock_contended (& self , state : State)
rules.rule: There must not be a `downgrade` in progress when calling `RwLock::unlock_contended`.

rules.name: unsafe fn downgrade (& self)
rules.rule: For safety, `RwLock::downgrade` must be called only when the lock is write-locked by the calling thread.

rules.name: unsafe fn downgrade_slow (& self , mut state : State)
rules.rule: For safety, the lock must be write-locked by the thread calling `downgrade_slow`.

rules.name: unsafe fn downgrade_slow (& self , mut state : State)
rules.rule: For safety, `state` must be a pointer to a node in a valid queue.

rules.name: unsafe fn downgrade_slow (& self , mut state : State)
rules.rule: For safety, there must be threads queued on the lock when `downgrade_slow` is called.

rules.name: unsafe fn unlock_queue (& self , mut state : State)
rules.rule: The current thread must hold the queue lock when calling `RwLock::unlock_queue`.

rules.name: unsafe fn unlock_queue (& self , mut state : State)
rules.rule: When calling `RwLock::unlock_queue`, `state` must be a pointer to a node in a valid queue.

rules.name: unsafe fn unlock_queue (& self , mut state : State)
rules.rule: There must be threads queued on the lock when calling `RwLock::unlock_queue`.

rules.name: unsafe fn new_in_place (parker : * mut Parker)
rules.rule: On UNIX, the `Parker` at `parker` must be constructed in place.

rules.name: unsafe fn new_in_place (parker : * mut Parker)
rules.rule: On UNIX, the new `Parker` must be created in place at `parker`.

rules.name: unsafe fn init_tid (& self)
rules.rule: Parker::init_tid must always be called from the same thread.

rules.name: unsafe fn init_tid (& self)
rules.rule: Parker::init_tid must be called before the state is set to PARKED.

rules.name: unsafe fn new_in_place (parker : * mut Parker)
rules.rule: The Parker constructed in place at `parker` must never be moved.

rules.name: unsafe fn run ()
rules.rule: For safety, `run` may only be called on thread exit, when there are no live references to TLS variables while they are destroyed.

rules.name: unsafe fn register_dtor (key : & 'static LazyKey)
rules.rule: For safety, `register_dtor` must be called at most once per key.

rules.name: unsafe fn run_dtors ()
rules.rule: For safety, `run_dtors` must only be called by the destructor callback in `guard`.

rules.name: unsafe fn get (& self) -> * const T
rules.rule: The `self` reference must remain valid until the TLS destructor is run.

rules.name: unsafe fn get (& self) -> * const T
rules.rule: The pointer returned by `get` must not be used after thread destruction has occurred.

rules.name: unsafe extern "C" fn destroy < T > (ptr : * mut u8)
rules.rule: `destroy<T>` must only be called at thread destruction.

rules.name: unsafe extern "C" fn destroy < T > (ptr : * mut u8)
rules.rule: When calling `destroy<T>`, `ptr` must point to an instance of `Storage` in the `Alive` state and be valid for accessing that instance.

rules.name: unsafe fn get_or_init (& self , i : Option < & mut Option < T > > , f : impl FnOnce () -> T) -> * const T
rules.rule: The `self` reference must remain valid until the TLS destructor is run.

rules.name: unsafe fn get_or_init (& self , i : Option < & mut Option < T > > , f : impl FnOnce () -> T) -> * const T
rules.rule: The pointer returned by `get_or_init` must not be used after reentrant initialization or thread destruction has occurred.

rules.name: unsafe extern "C" fn destroy < T > (ptr : * mut u8)
rules.rule: destroy<T> must only be called at thread destruction.

rules.name: unsafe extern "C" fn destroy < T > (ptr : * mut u8)
rules.rule: For destroy<T>, ptr must point to an instance of Storage<T, ()> and be valid for accessing that instance.

rules.name: unsafe fn try_initialize (key : Key , ptr : * mut Value < T > , i : Option < & mut Option < T > > , f : impl FnOnce () -> T ,) -> * const T
rules.rule: `key` must be the result of calling `self.key.force()`.

rules.name: unsafe fn try_initialize (key : Key , ptr : * mut Value < T > , i : Option < & mut Option < T > > , f : impl FnOnce () -> T ,) -> * const T
rules.rule: `ptr` must be the current value associated with `key`.

rules.name: unsafe fn new (lpwstr : * const u16) -> Option < Self >
rules.rule: For safety, `lpwstr` must point to a null-terminated wide string that lives at least as long as the returned `WStrUnits` struct.

rules.name: unsafe fn from_u32_unchecked (value : u32) -> CodePoint
rules.rule: For safety, `value` must be less than or equal to 0x10FFFF when calling `CodePoint::from_u32_unchecked`.

rules.name: unsafe fn from_bytes_unchecked (value : Vec < u8 >) -> Wtf8Buf
rules.rule: For safety, `value` must contain valid WTF-8.

rules.name: unsafe fn from_bytes_unchecked (value : & [u8]) -> & Wtf8
rules.rule: The byte slice `value` must contain valid WTF-8.

rules.name: unsafe fn from_mut_bytes_unchecked (value : & mut [u8]) -> & mut Wtf8
rules.rule: The bytes in `value` must be valid WTF-8 when calling `Wtf8::from_mut_bytes_unchecked`.

rules.name: unsafe fn spawn_unchecked < F , T > (self , f : F) -> io :: Result < JoinHandle < T > > where F : FnOnce () -> T , F : Send , T : Send ,
rules.rule: The caller must ensure that the thread spawned by `Builder::spawn_unchecked` does not outlive any references in the supplied closure `f` or its return type `T`. This may be guaranteed by calling `JoinHandle::join` before any referenced data is dropped, or by using only types with `'static` lifetime bounds—types containing no references or only `'static` references—for both `f` and `T`.

rules.name: unsafe fn park (& self)
rules.rule: `Thread::park(&self)` may only be called from the thread to which the handle belongs.

rules.name: unsafe fn park_timeout (& self , dur : Duration)
rules.rule: For safety, `Thread::park_timeout` may only be called from the thread to which `self` belongs.

rules.name: unsafe fn from_raw (ptr : * const ()) -> Thread
rules.rule: The pointer passed to Thread::from_raw must have been previously returned by Thread::into_raw; passing any other pointer is undefined behavior, even if the returned Thread is never accessed.

rules.name: unsafe fn from_raw (ptr : * const ()) -> Thread
rules.rule: If Thread::from_raw is called twice on the same raw pointer, the two resulting Thread instances must not both be dropped, as this can cause a double-free.
